Stage 01

Pre-Incorporation & Know-Your-Customer

UBO transparency, Apostille authentication chain, official name clearance restricted wordlist, and pre-incorporation statutory fee budget.

UBO Ultimate Beneficial Owner Screening Rules Official Registry Only

>=25% ownership / control

Applicable AML statute: Law 10/2010 of 28 April on the Prevention of Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing; Royal Decree 304/2014 of 5 May approving its implementing regulation; Royal Decree 609/2023 of 11 July establishing the Central Register of Beneficial Ownership; applicable provisions of the Spanish Commercial Code, Royal Legislative Decree 1/2010 approving the Capital Companies Act, Law 39/2015 on Common Administrative Procedure, EU Directive (EU) 2015/849 as amended, Regulation (EU) 2018/843, Regulation (EU) 2024/1624 where applicable, and Regulation (EU) 2015/847 on payer information.
Registered Agent & Physical Address Licensed Agent Required

A Spanish SL must have a registered office in Spain under the Capital Companies Act. A serviced or virtual office may be used for corporate domicile, correspondence, and certain administrative purposes only if the provider permits the activity, accepts official service, maintains reliable records, and the address is genuinely available to the company. It is not sufficient for regulated pharmaceutical manufacturing, handling, storage, quality-control, wholesale distribution, pharmacovigilance, or cold-chain operations. Manufacturing or distribution of botulinum-toxin medicinal products requires appropriate premises, qualified personnel, quality systems, good manufacturing or distribution practice compliance, controlled storage, traceability, and the relevant authorisations from the Spanish Agency of Medicines and Medical Devices (AEMPS) and, where applicable, autonomous-community authorities. A virtual office may therefore support a holding or preliminary administrative entity but cannot substitute for licensed operational premises.

✓ Partner licensed company-secretary channels provide local registered address and government mail forwarding.

Stage 02

Statutory Formation & Board Resolutions

Competent registry, governing statute, capital lockup rules, and first board resolution template.

Competent corporate registry

Registro Mercantil Central for company name certification; provincial Registro Mercantil where the registered office is located for substantive registration; formalisation before a Spanish notary.

Governing statute

Royal Legislative Decree 1/2010 of 2 July, approving the consolidated text of the Capital Companies Act (Ley de Sociedades de Capital): articles 19–25 (incorporation formalities), 58–64 (SL capital and contributions), 96–106 (registered office), 109–112 (appointment of directors), 210–213 (registry filing duties); supplemented by Royal Decree 1784/1996 (Commercial Registry Regulations).

Formation / constitutional filings

Escritura pública de constitución de sociedad de responsabilidad limitada (public incorporation deed), filed for registration in the provincial Commercial Registry.

Incorporation processing time

⚡ 31 business days (SOP sum)

Paid-up Capital & Blocked Account Regime Mandatory Capital Deposit & Lockup

No separate minimum capital requirement above the statutory SL threshold: subscribed capital must be at least €3,000 and fully paid at subscription. Cash contributions must be evidenced by a blocked bank deposit certificate issued at a Spanish credit institution in the company's name; in-kind contributions require an independent expert valuation report. The deposit is not held in an administrative escrow account and is released for corporate use after registration.

Funding & unlock path: Fire-safety project approval and certificate issued by the local fire service or autonomic civil-defence authority; structural load inspection and seismic conformity certificate by a qualified architect; occupational health-and-safety assessment under Ley 31/1995 including RD 486/1997 on workplaces and RD 664/1997 on biological agents; and AEMPS GMP site inspection clearance before commercial operation.

Paid-in capital rule: No separate minimum capital requirement above the statutory SL threshold: subscribed capital must be at least €3,000 and fully paid at subscription. Cash contributions must be evidenced by a blocked bank deposit certificate issued at a Spanish credit institution in the company's name; in-kind contributions require an independent expert valuation report. The deposit is not held in an administrative escrow account and is released for corporate use after registration.

Stage 03

Tax Identity & Indirect Tax

Tax authority e-portal, entity tax classification elections, VAT thresholds, and 0% export documentation chain.

Tax ID Application Infrastructure

Competent tax authority

Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT), including its Sede Electrónica. The competent regional tax administrations of the autonomous communities may administer certain transfer, inheritance, and local or ceded taxes, but Spanish national corporate income tax and VAT registration are administered principally by the AEAT.

E-government filing portal

A Spanish Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada must obtain a provisional Número de Identificación Fiscal (NIF) from the AEAT, generally through Form 036, after incorporation documentation is available and before commencing taxable activity. The application normally includes the public deed of incorporation, commercial registry filing or registration evidence, articles of association, registered address, identification of directors and authorized representatives, and powers of attorney where applicable. The provisional NIF must be converted into a definitive NIF after registration with the Commercial Registry and submission of the definitive registration evidence. Foreign shareholders, directors, and authorized representatives generally require Spanish NIFs; non-Spanish individuals may require an NIE. A foreign entity conducting taxable business in Spain without establishing a Spanish company may apply for a Spanish NIF through Form 036, usually submitting evidence of legal existence, tax residence, constitutional documents, representative authority, and certified translations or legalization where required. The Spanish VAT identification number is the Spanish NIF prefixed with ES. Registration in the Registro de Operadores Intracomunitarios (ROI) and inclusion in the VIES system must be requested through Form 036 when intra-Community supplies, acquisitions, or services require it. An EORI number must be obtained from the customs authority before importing or exporting goods. Registration for the Special Register of Monthly VAT Refunds, the Immediate Supply of Information system, or other special regimes requires separate eligibility and election procedures.

Tax ID type & application path: Entity_Level_Taxation — A Spanish Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada must obtain a provisional Número de Identificación Fiscal (NIF) from the AEAT, generally through Form 036, after incorporation documentation is available and before commencing taxable activity. The application normally includes the public deed of incorporation, commercial registry filing or registration evidence, articles of association, registered address, identification of directors and authorized representatives, and powers of attorney where applicable. The provisional NIF must be converted into a definitive NIF after registration with the Commercial Registry and submission of the definitive registration evidence. Foreign shareholders, directors, and authorized representatives generally require Spanish NIFs; non-Spanish individuals may require an NIE. A foreign entity conducting taxable business in Spain without establishing a Spanish company may apply for a Spanish NIF through Form 036, usually submitting evidence of legal existence, tax residence, constitutional documents, representative authority, and certified translations or legalization where required. The Spanish VAT identification number is the Spanish NIF prefixed with ES. Registration in the Registro de Operadores Intracomunitarios (ROI) and inclusion in the VIES system must be requested through Form 036 when intra-Community supplies, acquisitions, or services require it. An EORI number must be obtained from the customs authority before importing or exporting goods. Registration for the Special Register of Monthly VAT Refunds, the Immediate Supply of Information system, or other special regimes requires separate eligibility and election procedures.

Default Tax Classification & Elections

Default tax classification

Entity_Level_Taxation

Available election forms

Spain does not operate a general United States-style check-the-box election for classifying an SL as fiscally transparent or entity-taxed. An SL is ordinarily subject to Spanish Corporate Income Tax as a separate legal taxpayer. Available elections and regimes may include tax consolidation for qualifying corporate groups, the special regime for mergers and reorganizations, the Canary Islands special regimes where geographically applicable, the cash-accounting VAT regime, the monthly VAT refund regime, and other statutory incentive regimes subject to eligibility and timely notification. Spanish anti-hybrid mismatch rules implement applicable EU and OECD measures and can deny deductions, impose inclusion outcomes, or limit relief for hybrid instruments, hybrid entities, imported mismatches, reverse hybrids, and related-party arrangements. These rules are not elective and cannot be displaced by a private entity-classification election.

VAT / GST & 0% Export Zero-Rating

Standard VAT / GST rate

21%

Mandatory registration threshold (Nexus)

EUR 0. Spain has no general VAT turnover threshold below which a person carrying on an independent economic activity is automatically exempt from registration. A taxable person must generally register before commencing taxable activities, making taxable supplies, or carrying out relevant intra-Community or import transactions. Certain supplies may be exempt, zero-rated, or outside scope, but they do not create a general small-business registration threshold.

Export 0% zero-rating conditions

Exports of goods from the Spanish VAT territory to destinations outside the European Union may be exempt with the right to deduct input VAT when the goods leave the EU and the statutory exporter, purchaser, or intermediary conditions are satisfied. The supplier must retain a customs export declaration and reliable evidence of exit from the EU, normally an electronic export message or equivalent customs confirmation, together with commercial, transport, and payment records. Intra-Community supplies of goods may be exempt with the right to deduct when the goods are dispatched to another EU Member State, the recipient is identified for VAT in another Member State, the supplier performs the required reporting, and transport and recipient-status evidence are retained. Services are not ordinarily treated as exports merely because the customer is foreign. B2B services generally follow the customer-location rule and may be outside Spanish VAT where the customer is established outside Spain, subject to special place-of-supply rules for services connected with immovable property, admission, transport, passenger services, short-term vehicle hire, telecommunications, electronically supplied services, and other regulated categories. Input VAT refunds are claimed through periodic VAT returns, the monthly refund regime, or, for eligible non-established businesses, the EU electronic refund procedure or the non-EU refund procedure subject to reciprocity, minimum amounts, deadlines, and documentation requirements.

  • Spanish or EU customs export declaration, normally submitted electronically through the Automated Export System or applicable customs platform
  • EORI number of the exporter and relevant customs representative
  • Commercial invoice identifying the exporter, consignee, goods, value, Incoterms, and transaction terms
  • Packing list and product description, including batch, serial, and cold-chain information where relevant
  • Transport document, such as bill of lading, air waybill, or road consignment note
  • Electronic confirmation of exit from the EU customs territory or equivalent customs exit evidence
  • Import clearance or destination-country customs evidence where commercially or legally available
  • Evidence of payment, purchase order, sales contract, and customer identity sufficient to link the shipment to the export supply
  • Export licenses, permits, certificates, and controlled-goods documentation where required for pharmaceutical, medical, biological, or toxin-related products
  • VAT books, invoice records, and statutory accounting records supporting the reported zero-rated or exempt transaction
  • Inward remittance evidence only where required by a bank, financing arrangement, grant condition, or specific audit request; Spain does not impose a universal certificate of inward remittance as a general VAT zero-rating document

Spain does not currently apply a universal real-time pre-clearance requirement to every invoice. Taxpayers subject to the Immediate Supply of Information system (Suministro Inmediato de Información, SII), principally taxpayers with annual turnover exceeding EUR 6 million, VAT groups, and taxpayers opting into the monthly refund regime, must transmit specified invoice-record data electronically to the AEAT generally within four business days, subject to statutory exceptions. Electronic invoices must satisfy Spanish VAT invoice-content, authenticity, integrity, accessibility, and retention requirements. Public-sector electronic invoicing is mandatory for covered transactions through the FACe system. The Law on the Creation and Growth of Companies establishes a phased B2B electronic-invoicing framework, with implementing rules and effective dates dependent on publication and operation of the required regulations. Separately, Royal Decree 1007/2023 introduces certified billing-system requirements, including integrity, traceability, preservation, and anti-manipulation controls, commonly associated with the Veri*Factu framework; implementation dates and technical specifications must be confirmed for the relevant taxpayer and software. Non-compliance may lead to invoicing-system and tax penalties.

Spain has no general statutory requirement that export proceeds be repatriated within 180 days. Export receipts remain subject to ordinary banking, anti-money-laundering, foreign-exchange reporting, accounting, and transfer-pricing controls. If zero-rating or exemption is unsupported, the AEAT may assess unpaid VAT, statutory late-payment interest, and applicable tax penalties, with the taxpayer generally required to correct the VAT return and repay improperly recovered input VAT or refunds. Spanish General Tax Law penalties for serious or very serious VAT infringements may be calculated by reference to the unpaid or improperly refunded tax and can commonly range from 50% to 100% or more in aggravated cases, subject to the applicable offense, concealment, fraud, repetition, voluntary regularization, and cooperation rules. False invoices, fabricated exit evidence, customs fraud, smuggling, money laundering, or deliberate tax fraud may create additional administrative or criminal exposure. Customs authorities may recover import duties and import VAT, impose customs penalties under applicable Spanish and EU customs law, suspend simplified procedures, and refer serious conduct for criminal investigation. Statutory limitation periods, penalty reduction rules, interest, and voluntary-disclosure consequences must be assessed against the transaction record and the date of the relevant return or refund.

Stage 04

Banking & Treasury Architecture

Central-bank FX diagnosis, tier-1 local banks vs offshore digital EMI matrix, and KYC rejection defense guide.

Foreign Exchange Regime & Central Bank Policy

Current-account convertibility

The euro is fully convertible. Spain observes Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union Articles 63-66 on free movement of capital, so both current-account and capital-account transactions are liberalized without exchange controls. Profit remittance by an SL requires only approved audited financial statements, an equityholders' distribution agreement, updated beneficial-ownership registry filings, and the standard Bank of Spain statistical declaration; non-resident dividend withholding at 19% (reducible by treaty) applies, but there is no central-bank permission hurdle for repatriation. The only practical constraint for Chinese- or Latin-American-linked investors is the documentary proof of the lawful origin of funds under AML Law 10/2010.

Export proceeds surrender rules

No statutory surrender, forced conversion ratio, or repatriation timeline applies to Spanish exporters' proceeds in euros or foreign currency. Exporters may retain foreign currency indefinitely, but cross-border receipts and payments exceeding statutory thresholds must be reported to the Bank of Spain's balance-of-payments statistical channel (BE-web/Form T1/T4 electronic declarations). For botulinum toxin shipments, the AEMPS export authorization, the EUR.1/certificate-of-origin documentation and the commercial invoice must be retained to substantiate each reported transaction.

Central bank supervision: Banco de España (Bank of Spain) within the Eurosystem and the European Central Bank framework, together with the Ministry of Economy and the Directorate-General for International Trade and Investment (DGCOMEX) as the administrative authority for the foreign-investment and balance-of-payments statistical regime.

Offshore Digital Bank / EMI Whitelist

Cross-border EMI / Fintech rails Fit: High

Low feasibility for offshore (non-EU/EEA) digital EMI providers because PSD2 passporting does not extend to third-country entities and they cannot execute commercial letters of credit, a core clearing rail for cold-chain botulinum toxin batches. EU/EEA-licensed EMIs may passport into Spain under PSD2, but most decline High_Risk_Special_License pharmaceutical/biotech clients due to enhanced due-diligence costs, reputational exposure and the absence of LC/trade-finance infrastructure; an EMI-only treasury structure is therefore insufficient for the target payment rails.

Core KYC Rejection Triggers & Defense Dossier

Beneficial-ownership opacity: multi-tier non-EU shareholding chain, trusts, or nominee arrangements masking the ultimate owners.

Root cause: Beneficial-ownership opacity: multi-tier non-EU shareholding chain, trusts, or nominee arrangements masking the ultimate owners.

Defense evidence: Notarized corporate structure chart through to every UBO; signed identification and address proof per UBO in Ley 10/2010 and Real Decreto 304/2014 format; apostilled company-register extracts; sworn affidavit on lawful origin of capital; and matching Spain's centralized beneficial-ownership registry extract to the bank's Titularidad Real declaration.
Special-licence insufficiency: inability to evidence lawful manufacture, import, storage and distribution of botulinum toxin medicinal-aesthetics products.

Root cause: Special-licence insufficiency: inability to evidence lawful manufacture, import, storage and distribution of botulinum toxin medicinal-aesthetics products.

Defense evidence: Valid AEMPS (Agencia Española de Medicamentos y Productos Sanitarios) establishment and product authorizations; EU Good-Distribution-Practice (GDP) wholesale-distribution licence; GMP certificate covering fermentation and lyophilization; controlled-substance permits where applicable; ISIC 2100/NAICS 325414-specific import/export licences; and a Qualified Person (QP) certification letter.
Trade-provenance and pricing anomalies: high per-vial unit value, ES-to-Latin-America distribution triangulation, or inconsistent cold-chain documentation.

Root cause: Trade-provenance and pricing anomalies: high per-vial unit value, ES-to-Latin-America distribution triangulation, or inconsistent cold-chain documentation.

Defense evidence: Purchase-order-to-invoice audit trail; supplier/manufacturer agreements and chain-of-custody evidence; cold-chain temperature-monitoring logs with 3PL logistics contracts; batch-release certificates; transport and product-liability insurance policies; and export declarations, bills of lading/AWB and customs records matching each wire.
Source-of-wealth concerns on inbound capital injection from an offshore holding or newly formed foreign investor entity.

Root cause: Source-of-wealth concerns on inbound capital injection from an offshore holding or newly formed foreign investor entity.

Defense evidence: Three years of audited parent financial statements; investor relationship-bank reference letters; tax-residence certificates and CIT filings; origin-of-funds declaration aligned with Regulation (EU) 2015/847 wire-transfer Travel Rule data; and bank statements evidencing the lawful provenance of the remitting account.
Sanctions, PEP and adverse-media hits on UBOs, distributors or Latin-American counterparties in the aesthetics chain.

Root cause: Sanctions, PEP and adverse-media hits on UBOs, distributors or Latin-American counterparties in the aesthetics chain.

Defense evidence: Independent sanctions-screen clearances (UN, EU and OFAC consolidated lists) dated within 30 days, PEP-status declarations with public-source verification, adverse-media explanation letters supported by official court/tax records, a registered compliance firm's clearance certificate, and acceptance of a 12-month enhanced monitoring covenant.

Cross-Border Clearing Corridors & Settlement Fit

Shareholder capital enters Spain by SWIFT MT103 from the investor's bank to the SL's EUR IBAN at a licensed Spanish credit institution; no prior exchange authorization is required. The wire must carry a clear purpose code for capital subscription/contribution, and the receiving bank must hold a notarized equityholders' resolution, the updated BO-registry extract and the capital-increase public deed before applying funds. Post-close, the Bank of Spain statistical declaration applies; if the investor is non-EU/EEA and controls at least 10% of voting rights in this health-critical ISIC 2100 company, the Spanish FDI screening notification to DGCOMEX under Law 19/2003 (as amended by Royal Decree-Law 34/2020) may be required, and the AEMPS licence number should be cited on all cold-chain capital wires.Operational and small-value payments clear by SWIFT MT103 via SEPA/TARGET2 in euro; high-value cold-chain batch purchases (e.g., US-sourced botulinum toxin active substance) are settled by commercial letters of credit governed by UCP 600 through the bank's Nostro/correspondent network, with the target rails 'Cold_Chain_Wire' and 'Letter_Of_Credit' executed as documentary letters of credit or documentary collections. Each outbound wire must attach the DGCOMEX/BdE purpose code for goods or services, the AEMPS export authorization, the underlying commercial contract, and transport/customs documents to survive the bank's trade-compliance and sanctions screening; USD disbursements are hedged to EUR under the permitted instruments below.Plain-vanilla EUR/USD deliverable FX forward contracts executed with a European credit institution under ISDA or master forward agreements, EMIR-cleared or bilaterally margined.Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) limited to emerging-market currencies (Latin-American and CNH) where delivery of the local currency is restricted; must be conducted through a local or international bank with an EMIR-eligible offshore booking centre.EUR/USD cross-currency swaps (currency swaps) under an ISDA 2002 Master Agreement with credit support annex, centrally cleared for financial counterparties and eligible for hedge accounting under IFRS 9.

E-commerce / gateway settlement fit: Low feasibility for offshore (non-EU/EEA) digital EMI providers because PSD2 passporting does not extend to third-country entities and they cannot execute commercial letters of credit, a core clearing rail for cold-chain botulinum toxin batches. EU/EEA-licensed EMIs may passport into Spain under PSD2, but most decline High_Risk_Special_License pharmaceutical/biotech clients due to enhanced due-diligence costs, reputational exposure and the absence of LC/trade-finance infrastructure; an EMI-only treasury structure is therefore insufficient for the target payment rails.

Stage 06

Corporate Tax & Transfer Pricing

Corporate income tax (CIT), box-by-box return breakdown, dividend WHT, and director personal liability.

Statutory corporate income tax (CIT)

25%

Dividend withholding tax (WHT)

19% domestic Spanish withholding on dividends and other profit distributions to non-residents, subject to exemptions and treaty relief. The EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive exemption may eliminate withholding where the statutory ownership, holding-period, subject-to-tax, legal-form, beneficial-ownership and anti-abuse conditions are satisfied. The Spanish domestic participation exemption generally does not itself eliminate dividend withholding.

Mandatory Return Breakdown

Deadline: · Frequency:

File within the first 25 calendar days following the six-month period after the end of the fiscal year. For a calendar-year taxpayer closing on 31 December, the ordinary filing period is 1 July through 25 July of the following year. If the deadline falls on a non-business day, the applicable electronic filing rule extends it to the next business day.

Deadline: · Frequency:

The ordinary filing windows are 1 April through 20 April, 1 October through 20 October and 1 December through 20 December. The payment-on-account basis is generally either the prior-period tax liability method or the current-period taxable-base method, depending on statutory conditions and taxpayer status.

Deadline: · Frequency:

Generally filed within the same 25-calendar-day period following the six-month period after the consolidated tax period closes, subject to the applicable group-filing rules.

Transfer Pricing & Economic Substance

Master / Local File threshold: Spain does not use a single universal turnover threshold that removes all transfer-pricing obligations. Transactions with the same related person generally benefit from the documentation exemption only where the aggregate market value for the relevant transaction category does not exceed EUR 250,000 in the tax period, subject to exclusions and anti-abuse rules. A Local File is generally required for documented related-party transactions, with simplified documentation potentially available for entities with net turnover below EUR 45 million. A Master File is generally required for Spanish entities forming part of a multinational group, subject to statutory exclusions and group-specific documentation rules. Country-by-Country reporting generally applies to qualifying multinational groups with consolidated revenue of at least EUR 750 million.

Economic substance scope: Spain has no separate UAE-style Economic Substance Regulations regime. Substance is nevertheless material under Spanish transfer-pricing rules, the principal-purpose test, beneficial-ownership analysis, the general anti-abuse rule, controlled foreign company rules, anti-hybrid rules, interest limitation rules, treaty interpretation and permanent-establishment analysis. A Spanish SL manufacturing or handling botulinum-toxin aesthetic products should maintain genuine Spanish management, qualified personnel, premises, manufacturing or logistics capacity, quality and regulatory functions, decision-making records, risk control, inventory records, bank activity and commercial rationale. A company receiving royalties, service fees or financing without corresponding functions, assets and risks may be challenged as a conduit or non-substantive entity.

Fatal Compliance Red Lines & Director Liability

Corporate income tax evasion

Statutory sanction: Administrative penalties generally range from 50% to 150% of the unpaid tax, plus interest and collection costs. Criminal tax fraud may arise when the defrauded amount exceeds EUR 120,000 per tax period, with imprisonment generally from one to five years and fines; aggravated cases may carry two to six years' imprisonment and higher fines.

Director personal liability: Directors and de facto managers may incur civil, administrative and criminal liability. Courts may impose asset-restoration orders, disqualification from public subsidies or management, precautionary asset measures and, in criminal proceedings, travel restrictions or detention orders. A travel ban is not an automatic tax consequence.
False invoices and sham transactions

Statutory sanction: Tax adjustments, denial of deductions and input VAT, penalties, late-payment interest and potential criminal liability for tax fraud, accounting offenses, document falsification or commercial fraud.

Director personal liability: Directors who authorize, knowingly approve or facilitate sham transactions may face joint or subsidiary tax liability, civil restitution and criminal prosecution, including imprisonment where criminal thresholds are met.
Transfer-pricing manipulation

Statutory sanction: The AEAT may make a primary adjustment, impose documentation-related penalties, charge interest and make corresponding adjustments subject to statutory procedures. Failure to provide documentation or providing materially incorrect documentation can trigger specific penalties, generally linked to data or adjustment amounts and subject to statutory caps.

Director personal liability: Directors may become liable where deliberate concealment, abusive conduct, insolvency mismanagement or repeated non-compliance is established. Ordinary pricing disagreement does not by itself create criminal director liability.
Transfer-pricing documentation failure

Statutory sanction: Specific Spanish tax penalties may apply for missing, late, inaccurate or incomplete related-party documentation, in addition to income adjustments and interest. Country-by-Country reporting failures may attract separate penalties.

Director personal liability: Directors may face administrative liability through formal management-responsibility rules and insolvency or misconduct proceedings, particularly where the failure is intentional or contributes to unpaid tax.
Unlawful profit repatriation and withholding failure

Statutory sanction: The Spanish payer may be assessed for the unwithheld tax, interest and penalties. Treaty or EU exemptions can be denied where documentation, holding-period, subject-to-tax, anti-abuse or beneficial-ownership conditions are not met.

Director personal liability: Directors may incur subsidiary or joint liability where they deliberately cause withholding failures, frustrate collection or continue distributions while tax debts are unpaid.
Treaty abuse and conduit company

Statutory sanction: Denial of treaty or directive relief, reassessment at the domestic rate, interest, penalties and potential application of the Spanish general anti-abuse rule or principal-purpose test.

Director personal liability: Individuals knowingly implementing abusive arrangements may face tax, civil and, where deception or falsification is involved, criminal exposure. Corporate veil piercing is exceptional and requires legally recognized grounds.
Permanent establishment and place-of-effective-management risk

Statutory sanction: Spanish corporate income tax, non-resident income tax, VAT, payroll and withholding liabilities may be assessed, with interest and penalties for omitted registration and returns.

Director personal liability: Directors may be liable for deliberate concealment, false filings or collection obstruction; ordinary errors are generally addressed against the taxpayer rather than through automatic personal liability.
VAT fraud and carousel transactions

Statutory sanction: VAT assessment, interest and administrative penalties may apply; serious or organized fraud can result in criminal prosecution and asset seizure.

Director personal liability: Directors and beneficial owners involved in deliberate VAT fraud may face civil restitution, criminal fines, imprisonment and management disqualification.
Medical-product licensing and tax integrity failure

Statutory sanction: Regulatory sanctions may include product seizure, recall, suspension or revocation of authorization, business closure, substantial fines and criminal liability for serious public-health offenses. Tax deductions and customs treatment may also be challenged where transactions are unlawful or undocumented.

Director personal liability: Directors and responsible technical personnel may face civil liability for injury, administrative sanctions and criminal prosecution. Corporate limited liability does not protect intentional misconduct or statutory public-health offenses.
Customs undervaluation and origin misstatement

Statutory sanction: Import duty, import VAT, interest, customs penalties, seizure and possible criminal customs-fraud liability may apply. Customs authorities may disregard transfer-pricing values where valuation rules require adjustment.

Director personal liability: Directors, customs representatives and beneficial owners may incur joint or subsidiary liabilities where they knowingly submit false customs declarations or obstruct enforcement.
Anti-money laundering and terrorist-financing breach

Statutory sanction: Under Spanish AML legislation, serious and very serious infringements can result in significant fines, public disclosure, reprimands, temporary prohibitions and management sanctions. Criminal money laundering can carry imprisonment, fines and confiscation.

Director personal liability: Directors, compliance officers and beneficial owners may face personal administrative and criminal liability, asset freezing, confiscation, civil restitution and court-ordered travel restrictions in criminal proceedings.
Sanctions and export-control violation

Statutory sanction: Administrative fines, transaction prohibition, license revocation, asset freezing and criminal sanctions may apply under EU and Spanish sanctions, export-control and public-health rules.

Director personal liability: Knowing participation can lead to personal fines, imprisonment, disqualification, confiscation and civil liability for resulting losses.
Accounting and corporate-record falsification

Statutory sanction: Tax reassessment, accounting penalties, director disqualification, civil damages and criminal liability for accounting, commercial or document offenses may apply.

Director personal liability: Directors may be personally liable for creditor losses and unpaid tax in insolvency proceedings and may face imprisonment where intentional falsification satisfies criminal-law elements.
Insolvency and creditor-prejudice conduct

Statutory sanction: The insolvency may be classified as culpable, producing liability for damages, loss of rights, disqualification and possible coverage of the insolvency deficit, in addition to tax and criminal consequences.

Director personal liability: Directors and de facto directors may be ordered to restore assets, pay damages or cover all or part of the deficit and may face disqualification and criminal prosecution.
Unlawful dividend distribution

Statutory sanction: Recipients may be required to return improperly distributed dividends where they knew or should have known the distribution was unlawful. Directors may owe damages and face corporate-law sanctions.

Director personal liability: Directors approving unlawful distributions may be jointly liable for restitution and creditor losses; criminal exposure may arise if the distribution is part of fraud or asset concealment.
Employment, payroll and social-security evasion

Statutory sanction: Back payroll tax, social-security contributions, interest, administrative penalties and, for serious cases, criminal liability may apply.

Director personal liability: Directors may be jointly or subsidiarily liable for social-security and withholding debts where statutory management-failure conditions are satisfied.
Data, pharmacovigilance and regulated-record failure

Statutory sanction: Product-regulatory fines, recalls, authorization sanctions, data-protection fines and potential criminal public-health liability may apply.

Director personal liability: Directors and technical officers may incur personal civil, administrative and criminal liability for intentional or negligent regulatory failures causing patient or market harm.
